name: Yarrow

schedule.notes: Surface-sow; needs light to germinate. Press in, don't bury.
Tolerates a light frost once hardened off.
Cut whole stems when flowers are fully open. Repeat-blooms if cut hard.

harvest.cues: Flat-topped flower clusters fully open and showing color. Cut stems to the base for a second flush.
harvest.storageNotes: Excellent dried — hang in bundles upside down. Holds color for months in arrangements.

varieties.name: Common Yarrow
varieties.notes: White flat clusters, ferny gray-green foliage. The classic medicinal form.

varieties.name: Moonshine
varieties.notes: Bright lemon-yellow, silvery foliage, compact 18 to 24 in. Hybrid; doesn't spread.

varieties.name: Summer Pastels Mix
varieties.notes: Pink, peach, lavender, cream — easy from seed, first-year flowering.

notes: Thrives on neglect; rich or wet soil makes it floppy and disease-prone. Spreads by rhizome — the wild white form can colonize, hybrids stay put. Lacy foliage and umbel flowers are top pollinator habitat for hoverflies and parasitic wasps that eat aphids.
